niya: Postmortem follow-up: recurring overnight model-load spikes -> intermittent 503s for ~2-4m. We need a single-page runbook and a tiny triage tool that can be run from the on-call laptop. Ship in 2 weeks.

niya: High level actions (short):
A) Compact runbook with explicit escalation ladder (0m channel / 3m pager / 10m phone). owner: keisha. due: 2024-12-09
B) Triage CLI `load-triage.sh` with health, p50/p95 model-load, and logs-grab. owner: omar. due: 2024-12-09
C) Cron warmup: k8s CronJob to warm models at 23:45 and 02:15. owner: eng-platform. due: 2024-12-11
D) Fallback route: add automatic partial-traffic failover to standby model variant on high model-load error rate. owner: niya. due: 2024-12-16
E) CI smoke gate: 5 quick warm requests, mean latency < 300ms, no 5xx. owner: keisha + eng-sre. due: 2024-12-16

niya: Minimal triage snippet to include in `load-triage.sh` (no tokens hardcoded):
# health check
curl -fsS https://api.redwood-infer/health || echo "health: FAIL"
# model load metrics (p50/p95) - script should read METRICS_KEY from env or vault
curl -sS "https://metrics/api?query=model_load_latency_p50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $METRICS_KEY" | jq .
curl -sS "https://metrics/api?query=model_load_latency_p95" -H "Authorization: Bearer $METRICS_KEY" | jq .
# recent runtime logs (last 300 lines)
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime --tail=300

omar: I'll own `load-triage.sh`. Plan: implement `--quick` (health+p50), `--full` (adds p95 and logs), and `--dry-run`. Script will prompt for METRICS_KEY if missing. Will put a note: never hardcode secrets.

keisha: I'll write the compact runbook. Top of doc will be a 6-step checklist: detect -> confirm metrics -> collect logs -> short mitigation (fallback route) -> engage platform -> postmortem notes. Appendix will include exact `kubectl` and restart hints for SREs. Will create `docs/playbooks/model-load-quickplay.md`.

sre-bot: Incident filed INC-2024-399. Epic created: RINF-601.

oncall-bot: Tabletop rehearsal scheduled: 2024-12-07 16:00 UTC.

omar: Quick question: for the metrics queries do we want p50/p95 only, or include error-rate queries? I suggest p50/p95 + request_error_rate for triage.

niya: Agree. Keep triage lightweight: p50/p95 + error rate. Add guidance in runbook for when to collect p99/p999 for deeper analysis.

keisha: For escalation ladder, proposed wording: 0m post to #incidents-model-load, 3m page eng-sre, 10m page eng-platform and notify manager on call. I'll include phone numbers in a vault link.

omar: I'll post a first-pass gist of `load-triage.sh` tomorrow morning. Will include unit tests for metrics parsing.

keisha: I'll open playbook PR Monday and reference RINF-601. Please link your PRs to the epic so I can approve.

niya: I'll gate reviews until triage script + cronjob PRs are linked. After PRs land, we'll run the tabletop with an on-call engineer and gather friction notes. Keep playbook prescriptive and "do this first" at the top.

oncall-bot: Reminder: tabletop added to calendar.

omar: noted.

keisha: noted.

niya: Closing: keep language direct, top-of-doc action-first, expand in appendix. If anything looks like it needs automation, create a follow-up ticket instead of bloating the runbook.

omar: :thumbsup:

keisha: :white_check_mark:
